case_title: Prakash Nayi @ Sen v. State of Goa
accused_occupation: Worked at a store (per prosecution case); otherwise not stated
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (the victim was working at the store where the accused attacked him; no personal connection described)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (defence raised under IPC s.84)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW2); medical evidence (hospital treatment records, doctors' depositions and certificates); conduct evidence; family witness evidence on prior treatment
mitigating_circumstances: Prior treatment for schizophrenia-type illness before the incident; later fitness to stand trial; subsequent recovery (noted by the court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302; sentence not stated
high_court_outcome: Conviction upheld by Division Bench, Bombay High Court at Goa (CRLA No.63 of 2006, dated 02.06.2008)
neutral_facts: On the morning of 14 May 2004, at about 6:00 a.m., the accused attacked the victim with an iron locking plate inside a store where the victim was working. The store belonged to the brother of the accused's grandfather. The prosecution alleged there was no motive, no provocation and no premeditation. An eyewitness saw the incident. After the assault, the accused took the object out of the store, walked to a nearby bus stand, returned and left the object in the shop, then went back to the bus stand and sat on a chair without attempting to leave. Before the incident, the accused had been an in-patient at a government hospital in Bhiwani, Haryana, from 17 to 26 November 2003. The records noted anxiety neurosis with reactive depression, symptoms of acid peptic disease and mild hypertension. The treatment given was akin to that for schizophrenia, and the medicine Thioril was prescribed. After the incident, a government doctor examined the accused. She later certified that the accused had chronic schizophrenia, probably from around age 14 or 15, and was not fit to stand trial. A later certificate, issued after in-patient treatment, stated the accused could stand trial. Her statement was recorded about sixteen years after the occurrence. An uncle of the accused testified about the earlier treatment. A relative of the accused's grandfather who was examined found no abnormality. The doctor who physically examined the accused after the incident stated the accused was mentally well.
physical_harm: Death of the victim caused by assault with an iron locking plate
premeditation_planning: No finding of premeditation or planning; the prosecution case was that the attack was without provocation or premeditation
key_evidence_accepted: Evidence of the Government doctor (AW1/DW1) on schizophrenia and the certificate of unfitness to stand trial; evidence of AW2 on prior treatment; the fact of prior treatment
witness_credibility: Court found the Government doctor's evidence withstood cross-examination and should have been accepted; the fact of prior treatment was undisputed and corroborated by AW2; the courts below wrongly disregarded this evidence
post_offence_conduct: Per prosecution case: took the object out, returned it to the shop, went back to the bus stand and sat without attempting to leave. The court did not rely on this conduct; it said the conduct was ignored by the courts below
bail_history: Not stated (a bail application was considered at trial; outcome not stated)
trial_duration: offence: 14.05.2004; trial judgment: 25.07.2006; High Court: 02.06.2008; Supreme Court: 12.01.2023
legal_representation: Appellant: Aftab Ali Khan (Supreme Court Legal Services Committee) with associates; State counsel not stated
investigation_status: Not stated (trial was conducted; investigation and charge sheet details not given)
procedural_irregularity: Courts below did not discuss the prior treatment or accept the doctors' evidence; the Supreme Court called for a report from the District and Sessions Judge, Bhiwani, because the prescription and other documents could not be deciphered
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC (25.07.2006). High Court: conviction upheld (02.06.2008). Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside and accused acquitted
prosecution_argument: Not stated (the judgment does not record State submissions)
defence_argument: Plea of insanity under IPC s.84: the accused was of unsound mind at the time of the act, supported by evidence of schizophrenia and prior treatment, so the accused is entitled to the benefit of s.84
legal_principle_applied: Legal (not medical) insanity test under IPC s.84; burden on accused discharged on preponderance of probability (Evidence Act s.105 read with s.8); conduct before, during and after the offence considered; CrPC Chapter XXV reasoning
precedent_relied_upon: Surendra Mishra v. State of Jharkhand (2011) 11 SCC 495; Hari Singh Gond v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2008) 16 SCC 109; Bapu @ Gajraj Singh v. State of Rajasthan (2007) 8 SCC 66; Dahyabhai Chhaganbhai Thakkar v. State of Gujarat AIR 1964 SC 1563; Devidas Loka Rathod v. State of Maharashtra (2018) 7 SCC 718
judicial_mitigating_factors: Not applicable to sentencing; court weighed prior insanity indicated by prior treatment, the doctor's evidence, and the later fitness to stand trial as grounds for acquittal
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; pending applications disposed of
